title.en: Sources of energy: food, fuel, electricity, Sun, wind and water

text.en: The teacher asks who ate breakfast, then asks the class to stretch, jump and run on the spot. How are you able to move?

We get energy to move from the food we eat. Animals also need energy to run, fly and swim and they get it from food. Food is a source of energy for all living things.
Fuel is another source. Cooking gas is a fuel, and in some places people burn wood or coal, which makes smoke and pollution.
Diya activity: a wick with no oil burns out quickly while one with oil burns longer, because the oil is the fuel. We use fuels for cooking, lighting diyas and running vehicles.
Electricity runs fans, lights and machines and gives movement, sound, light and heat. It makes industries run, but can be dangerous if used carelessly.
Safe use: do not touch plugged wires, do not put fingers or pens in sockets, stay away from broken wires and fallen poles, do not play near electric boxes or transformers, and tell an adult if something looks unsafe.
Most electricity comes from burning coal which pollutes the air. Other sources produce electricity without pollution.
Pinwheel, magnifying glass and water wheel activities show that wind, the Sun and water can make things work. The Sun is the main source of energy for life on Earth.
Solar panels turn sunlight into electricity, windmills spin to make electricity and falling water can generate it. This is called clean energy.
Traders from Gujarat and Tamil Nadu once sailed to Africa, Arabia and Southeast Asia using the wind in sails. Gharaats, or watermills in the hills, grind grain with flowing water.
Cochin International Airport in Kerala was the world's first airport powered entirely by solar energy.

problem.en: Name the source of energy: running child, burning diya, drying papad.

text.en: A running child gets energy from food.
A diya burns oil, which is fuel.
A papad dries in the Sun's heat.

prompt.en: Name sources of energy and say which are clean.

points.en: Food, fuel and electricity give energy.
Sun, wind and water give clean energy.
